CH 3: IDEAL STAT LINES
Every piece of gear has “Stat Lines” that comes on it. These Stat Lines can be changed by using “Synch Stones” or other pieces of Gear of the equivalent grade (Yellow/Unique Synch Stones for Yellow/Unique gear). If you use lower grade Synch Stones (Yellow/Unique Synch Stone for an Orange/Heroic piece of gear, you will have a 10% chance for the stat to get rerolled - never do this).
Synch Stones are obtained via Substance Morphing either Synch Stone Fragments (mainly obtained by running dungeons) or any Yellow/Unique Gear piece.

You can get additional levels on skills via gear Stat Lines, Daevanion Board, and Arcana. You can select up to 3 Specialty Perks that are selectable only when reaching a certain level indicated by the number on the icon. You will have to equip the Specialty Perk into an open slot. Level 20 unlocks the 3rd slot.
Every class has key Level 20 Active Skills that are a must for the build to truly come online (will try and add a written Class Guide section to the doc). With Stigma Skills, you get the benefit of all Perks as long as you unlock them with levels. Stigma Skills use Stigma Shards to level and can be leveled up to 20 for the final Perk. After the Chapter 1, level 50 update, you can level Stigma Skills to 25 with the last 5 levels coming from golden Superior Stigma Shards. 
Stigma Shards are obtained by combining “Unstable Stigma Shards” that you’ll get from a variety of PVE content or directly from Abyss Points, a currency in Aion 2. Abyss Points are mainly obtained from Supply Request, Daily Duties, Weekly Commands (Contract-like quests), and farming players or mobs in the Abyss.
Superior Stigma Shards are obtained when leveling from 45 to 50, and additional Superior Stigma Shards can be obtained from getting other Stigma skills to lvl 20. You get 1 Superior Stigma Shard for every lvl 20 Stigma skill. When everything is maxed, you can have 3 skills at lvl 25, 1 skill at lvl 23, and the rest at lvl 20. 
Key Stigma Skills offer a lot of power when leveled. Generally these Stigma Skills offer major buffs and increase key Passive Skills amplifying both Damage and Support. Supports especially can be gatekept by lacking specific Stigma Skill levels (IE: Undefeated Mantra, Light of Protection) as they significantly boost group performance.

Step 1
Level your board to 10 and ignore the stats you get, do not lock any line until you do this
The exception to the above is:
If progression on global is too slow to the point where level 10 isn’t possible or practical to wait for 
You get a high yellow or orange BIS stat roll on Line 4 (all boards, bis stats are listed below)
Saving until level 10 gives you the highest chance to roll the highest grade lines
Step 2
After hitting level 10 on a board, “Analyze” (roll) it with no stats locked until you roll the BIS stats on Line 4 across all boards
Highest Prio Line 4 Boards are Special (Double Chance) and Varian (Front/Back Damage Boost) followed by Fera (Weapon Damage Boost) and Cogni (Critical Damage Boost)
Some people settle for lower % rolls on their Line 4 rolls for their first preset then work on higher % rolls on a second preset. 
Keep in mind a high Yellow roll can be higher than a low Orange roll
Additional Notes: You can do this by using the Auto Analysis and selecting Unique (or Heroic) Double Chance on Lines 3 and 9. It is not possible to roll lower than a Unique on Double Chance.

CH 11: HOW STATS WORK (DAMAGE FORMULA)
This chapter will include a full breakdown of how all the stats work including detailed formulas. Some of these equations are not known to anyone yet and are becoming public for the first time with this doc. 
I want to give a special shoutout to a well-recognized Korean Youtuber “Aion Research Lab” and his friends for discovering a lot of the formulas and equations listed out in this section. I spent a lot of time discussing numbers with him and it is STILL a work in progress…understandably so, considering the amount of sheer stats and convolution Aion 2 is with Damage. 
Updates will be made on any new discoveries including fixes, but until then this is the most accurate up-to-date info we have on how all the stats work. I’ve tried my best to lay this out in the easiest to understand way while preserving the details.
“Aion Research Lab” YouTube Channel Link
Kanon credits Aion Research Lab and his friends for these equations and describes the work as ongoing. First-person discovery and testing claims below remain attributed to that source.
Source attribution
—
End-game Stat Value
The following shows the damage efficiency for offensive stats based on current end-game Korea (on an ideal build) which is currently at the start of Season 1 (Start of level 50 and Lava Heart armor introduction). These stats also incorporate support buffs.
Generally speaking, diminishing returns are a thing. This means the values below will be different for Global launch (as well as future KR since more stats are added) considering we will have less stats, therefore less diminishing return impact. There will be a greater discrepancy with some stats for global launch. For example, Front/Back Damage Boost starts at a base value of 0% vs Critical Damage starting at 50%. The first 10% added to both stats favor Front/Back Damage Boost due to diminishing returns.
Also keep in mind certain classes have access to some buffs which diminish the value of certain stats the more you stack them (for example, the Critical Damage Boost stat with Gladiator).
Before we dive into the numbers, quick explanation on…
How Diminishing Returns Work using Double Chance Efficiency Example
What is Double Chance?
A: It gives you a certain chance to deal 2× damage.
If my normal damage is 1, then when Double Chanceprocs, the damage becomes 2.
How much stronger does 1% Double Chance make you?
Imagine that you have a 1% chance for your salary to be doubled.
If your salary is 1,000,000 won, then over 100 paychecks:
1,000,000 won × 100 = 100,000,000 won + 1,000,000 won
Since this represents receiving your salary 100 times, divide the total by 100 to find out how much you receive on average per paycheck.
My normal damage is 1, and when Double Chance procs, it becomes 2.
Double Chance 0% → 1%
How much does my DPS increase?
A: 1.01 → 1% DPS increase
Double Chance 0% → 2%
How much does my DPS increase?
A: 1.02 → 2% DPS increase
Double Chance 0% → 50%
How much does my DPS increase?
A: 1.5 → 50% DPS increase
Double Chance 1% → 2%
How much does my DPS increase?
A: 0.99%
At 1% Double Chance: 101 total damageAt 2% Double Chance: 102 total damage
So going from 101 → 102 is approximately a 0.99% actual DPS increase.
Practical Calculation
At 80% Double Chance, how efficient is another +1% Double Chance?
Assumptions:
Double Chance Resistance: 30%
 보빛 + 대징 support buffs: +12% Double Chance
The Korean passive shorthand is retained as written; no expansion is supplied by this chapter. The support buff and boss resistance assumptions are part of this example.
Untranslated source shorthand
80% Double Chance → 62% Final Double Chance
Now, how much DPS do you gain going from:
62% → 63% Double Chance?
If your base damage is 1 and you attack 100 times:
63 attacks deal 2 damage from Double Chance.
37 attacks deal 1 damage.
Therefore:
62% Double Chance = 162 total damage63% Double Chance = 163 total damage
Answer: 0.617% DPS increase
So:
+1% Double Chance = approximately +0.617% actual DPS at this point.

Keep in mind this stat has a base starting value @ 50%
Larger variance due to Class passives that impact Crit rate and damage
The above values based on:
Classes with Critical Damage buffs will be around 120% (≈ 0.4% range)
Classes without will be around 90% (≈ 0.6% range)

Accuracy & Block/Parry 
Accuracy ensures your attack lands as a clean hit negating a Block/Parry 1:1. If your Accuracy covers the exact amount of Block a target has, you will land 100% of your attacks.

In PVP, Damage will be reduced by 1% of your Defense value

The Defense after Penetration is 100 (200 Defense - 100 Penetration)

Damage Tolerance and Endurance are both highly effective Defensive stats. Damage Tolerance directly reduces Damage Boost against you while Endurance reduces your final damage taken by half.
The source later clarifies that the displayed Endurance percentage is the chance to take half damage, not a permanent halving of every hit.

Source recommendations, first-person statements, and testing claims are Kanon’s. Figures are captured examples rather than universal costs or ideal builds.

Efficiency values assume an ideal KR end-game build at the start of Season 1, level 50 and Lava Heart armor, including support buffs. Global launch, future KR, class buffs and diminishing returns can change these values.
Damage Formula
English:
[[[((Pure Attack × Weapon Damage Boost) × Multi-Hit × Power Shard) + Attack Bonus) × Attack Increase % + PvE Attack Power + Boss Attack Power + Species Attack Power + Front/Back Attack Power] × Skill Coefficient] − [(Defense − Penetration) × 0.1]] × (Damage Boost + PvE Damage Boost + Boss Damage Boost + Species Damage Boost) × Critical Damage Boost × Double × Front/Back Damage Boost × Skill Additional Damage = Final Damage
The source’s mixed and unmatched brackets and percentage conventions remain unresolved. Multi-hit placement is explicitly unconfirmed despite its displayed position. No calculator or repaired grouping is inferred.
Literal source formula and uncertainty
(*0.1 multiplier after Defense-Pen is 0.01 in PVP)
This formula has been tested extensively and IS the closest damage formula we currently have - everything except for the *Multi-hit placement is confirmed.  
*Multi-hit - The exact placement of Multi-hit needs to be tested more to 100% confirm its placement on the equation, there’s a chance it could be outside Attack Increase. Will update and remove this bullet once confirmed
This formula is public for the very first time with this doc…not because it’s some hidden secret, but because it was very difficult to figure out and simply put, no one has yet. There have been some general damage buckets posted and understood but this is the first detailed, specific formula that fully answers the why and how much. Math heads and theory crafters, here’s your baseline…
Important - What is “Pure Attack”?
“Pure Attack” is not an official stat in the game. It’s a label created to categorize the Attack that gets directly multiplied by Weapon Damage Boost. There are a lot of different types of “Attack” stats in-game but they are spread across the equation.
You can test the above by calculating the total Attack you get from your Weapon and removing it along with your Weapon Damage Boost % and see what the “Attack” value shows under your Stat Info > Main Stats page. The “Attack” value on here does not consider Weapon Damage Boost%
The stats that fall under “Pure Attack” is as follows:
Weapon Attack
Guard Attack
Accessories Attack
Attack Stat Lines
Manastone/Soulstone Attack
Closet 
Further Detail
Outside of “Pure Attack” the rest of the “Attacks” are added together starting from PVE Attack in the equation above. Because this added after Attack Increase the value is less than Pure Attack. When it comes to the flat “Attack” stats the value order is:
Tier 1 
Attack (Pure Attack)
Max Attack (Pure Attack)
Attack Bonus (within Attack Increase)
Tier 2
PVE Attack
Boss Attack
Tier 3 (Conditional)
Front/Back Attack
Species Attack
Critical Attack
Tier 3 stats are the worst considering they do not fall under “Pure Attack” and only get added to PVE/Boss Attack upon condition. Species being specific to mob type.
